ctx.x: Yes. Well, as I say, he held that at the -- the Baby Lawrence funeral idea at the Church of Emmanuel up there on 88th and -- I'm glad that you asked that -- and Lexington, you know. And one of the tap dancers ranks came out, you know, a line of them, you know, the ones that was in retirement. They came, you know. And they were in the parish, you know.

So, and their way of -- what you say -- giving the dead to the rest, you see -- this they rank got up, you see. See, and in the rank was one of the Four Badmen which was known as Peg-Leg Bates, see. And he got up and there was someone in -- yeah, Harold Kromer, the jazz monitor. He was there. I know he got up. And Lon Chaney.

Well, it was like some kind of squad, do you understand? A rank I'd say. I like to say a rank because that's what the guard officiates in the world, you see. And there was some speakers, you see. See, that's to just name a few of them. There was this -- one of Baby Lawrence's proteges -- I'm quite sure, but he didn't get enough of the tap dancer's dream, you know. He was very touched by it. He's still with us, you see. That's Bunny Briggs. And another great friend, you see, but we lost him, you see. See, they all…
